target.title: fix(agents): propagate Retry-After from Anthropic transport to session auto-retry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where users would experience rapid consecutive auto-retry failures and exhaust their retry attempts without honoring the provider's requested cooldown when the Anthropic API rate limits the connection (HTTP 429). The `anthropic-messages` transport previously dropped the HTTP status and `Retry-After` metadata from the error. Additionally, fixes a potential edge case where malformed or excessive `Retry-After` values from upstream proxies could permanently hang sessions for days by introducing a 5-minute hard cap on session wait time.

## Why This Change Was Made
This change updates the Anthropic transport stream handler to extract the `status` and `Retry-After` headers from failing provider responses and embed them in the thrown `ProviderHttpError`. The session manager's `prepareRetry` logic is updated to check for `retryAfterSeconds` on failing assistant messages and apply a `Math.max(baseBackoff, retryAfterSeconds * 1000)` delay before the next attempt, explicitly clamped to a maximum ceiling of 5 minutes (`300_000ms`) to protect against rogue upstream values.

## User Impact
When encountering Anthropic rate limits, OpenClaw will now correctly wait for the duration specified by the API instead of immediately failing after rapidly attempting retries. Users experiencing momentary rate limits will see a seamless recovery after the required cooldown, while being protected from unbounded hangs.

## Evidence

- Verified behavior from stub-provider transport-to-session path: `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` (propagates HTTP 429 status and `Retry-After` header to the assistant message result) and `agent-session.retry.test.ts` (consumes the metadata and computes backoff correctly).
- Added focused regression coverage for normal, excessive, non-finite, and absent `Retry-After` header values.
- Below is the live terminal proof of the session clamping the transport delay correctly:

```text
$ pnpm test:changed
✓ src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts (216 tests)
  ✓ propagates HTTP 429 status and Retry-After header to the assistant message result
✓ src/agents/sessions/agent-session.retry.test.ts (6 tests)
  ✓ honors Retry-After headers and emits auto_retry_start with the requested delay
  ✓ uses base delay backoff when no Retry-After is provided
  ✓ caps excessive Retry-After values to the 5-minute session maximum
  ✓ caps non-finite Retry-After values to the 5-minute session maximum

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  222 passed (222)

target.title: fix(process): bound Windows exec timeout cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Fixes an issue where users running a foreground `exec` command on Windows could wait roughly 10–12 seconds after an overall or no-output deadline before receiving the timeout result.**
- **Affected surface / workflow:** production `createExecTool` host execution on Windows and child-process supervisor cleanup.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** Windows timeout cancellation was sent through a graceful phase even though Windows has no catchable SIGTERM equivalent, delaying the eventual tree hard-kill. The first patch then bounded all post-exit stream waits, which could truncate output from ordinary descendants retaining inherited stdout/stderr.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** timeout results return promptly without changing the normal Windows output-drain contract or silently dropping late descendant output.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** Windows overall/no-output deadlines immediately request tree-aware `SIGKILL`; the child adapter's 250 ms forced stream settlement is armed only after an explicit hard-kill request and observed exit. Ordinary child exit continues waiting for stdout/stderr drain or the real `close` event.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** it separates the forced timeout/hard-kill lifecycle from normal process completion instead of applying a global post-exit watchdog. The timeout path remains bounded while normal retained pipes remain lossless.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** the supervisor owns timeout policy and chooses immediate hard-kill for Windows deadlines; the child adapter owns bounded settlement only after its `kill("SIGKILL")` boundary has been crossed.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** no public API, config, schema, dependency, lockfile, PTY behavior, Unix graceful-cancel behavior, manual-cancel grace period, or captured-output limit changed.
- **Root cause:** timeout policy and ordinary output draining were incorrectly coupled by a post-exit watchdog; the repair gates forced settlement on an explicit hard-kill lifecycle state.
- **Scope boundary:** only Windows deadline cancellation and Windows post-SIGKILL settlement change; normal child exit, Unix signaling, PTY execution, manual-cancel grace, APIs, config, schema, defaults, and dependencies remain unchanged.
- **Source-of-truth boundary:** `supervisor.ts` decides why and when cancellation becomes a Windows hard kill; `child.ts` observes that explicit hard-kill request and alone owns the bounded stream-settlement fallback.
- **Related open PR scan:** the referenced #85865 is the prior merged process-supervisor change this PR corrects; no separate public-contract implementation is introduced or duplicated.
- **Out of scope:** redesigning process supervision, changing public process/tool contracts, changing Unix cancellation, or applying forced settlement to ordinary exit.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: availability` / existing `merge-risk: 🚨 other`, because this touches foreground process completion and captured output.
- **Risk explanation:** an over-broad fallback can either delay timeout completion or truncate retained stdout/stderr. The implementation therefore requires both Windows and explicit `SIGKILL`, plus observed child exit, before the 250 ms settlement timer can arm.
- **Why acceptable:** the production timeout E2E retains the prior ~2.5-second result, the live ordinary-exit E2E retains descendant output beyond the former cutoff, and separate regressions lock both sides of the lifecycle boundary.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** focused process-lifecycle change. The forced stream destroy remains Windows-only and hard-kill-only; ordinary execution preserves the existing output contract.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** receive Windows timeout results in about 2.3 seconds wall time for a 0.2-second deadline while still receiving output written by descendants after the direct child exits.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** normal stdout/stderr draining, Unix SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation, manual cancellation, process-tree signaling, and exit-state reporting.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no external provider/channel was involved or needed. Validation used the real local Windows production `createExecTool` path. The repository requests Node >=22.19 while this Windows host has Node 22.17; the required combined process command therefore retains one unrelated Linux OOM-wrapper assertion failure on Windows, disclosed below.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows 10 x64, Node.js v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- **Commands run after this patch:** production `createExecTool({ host: "gateway", security: "full", ask: "off", allowBackground: false })` for (1) `node -e "setInterval(() => {}, 1000)"` with `timeout: 0.2` and (2) a real parent process that exits after spawning a detached descendant retaining inherited stdout/stderr and writing both streams 750 ms later; focused Vitest process/exec suites; local `pnpm check:changed` core/coreTests lanes; `git diff --check`.
- **Key results / observations:** current-main before-fix proof was 11,642 ms wall (`durationMs: 10,595`). A supervisor-only diagnostic variant was still 6,590 ms wall (`durationMs: 5,685`) and was rejected. After the required latest-main sync, final hard-kill-scoped settlement returned `overall-timeout`/`SIGKILL` in 2,526 ms wall (`durationMs: 1,863`). The post-sync ordinary-exit live proof completed in 3,112 ms wall with exit 0 and retained exactly `parent-before-exit`, `descendant-stdout`, and `descendant-stderr`; descendant output was emitted 750 ms after parent exit, beyond the old 250 ms cutoff.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** `RF-001` waiting-on-author — addressed by this update and fresh proof. `RF-002` — fixed: forced closure is hard-kill-only and a normal descendant-held-pipe regression was added. `RF-003` — fixed: ordinary exit no longer destroys stdout/stderr; live output-integrity proof retained both late streams. `RF-004` — fixed with the narrow mechanical lifecycle split, preserving timeout timing. `RF-005` — fixed at `child.ts`: explicit `SIGKILL` is now required before forced Windows settlement can arm. `RF-006` — required command executed: supervisor 9/9 and all changed child lifecycle tests passed; the broad combined run was 30 passed/1 unrelated pre-existing Linux OOM-wrapper assertion failure on this Windows host. `RF-007` — exec runtime integration passed 38/38. `RF-008` — local `check:changed` core/coreTests lanes exited 0, including typechecks and repository guards.
- **Regression guardrail:** unit coverage proves ordinary Windows exit remains pending beyond 1 second, preserves open streams, captures late stdout/stderr, and settles only after drain; separate coverage proves explicit hard-kill settlement remains pending at 249 ms and settles/destroys streams at 250 ms. Production E2E covers both timeout timing and ordinary descendant-held inherited pipes.
- **Patch quality notes:** two-file corrective delta on top of the existing four-file PR; no dependencies, lockfile, config, API, suppressions, skipped tests, or changelog changes. The prior remote CI failure was unrelated (`doctor-health-contributions` expected `local-audio-acceleration`, outside all process paths).
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** high; the ClawSweeper truncation blocker is directly reproduced and covered while the original timeout improvement remains within the prior ~2.3-second production timing.

target.title: fix(imessage): apply authoritative projection in anchorless recovery
target.body:
Fixes openclaw/openclaw#104136

## What Problem This Solves

`repairIMessageConversationAnchor()` recovered conversation anchors from exact-GUID `messages.history` rows but only overlaid `chat_id` / `chat_guid` / `chat_identifier`. It preserved stale notification `sender`, `destination_caller_id`, and `is_from_me`, which could:

1. Route a direct reply at the local iMessage identity instead of the remote peer.
2. Dispatch an outgoing row as inbound when history says `is_from_me: true` but the broken notification said `false`.

## Changes

- Build a complete **authoritative recovery projection** from exact-GUID history rows (sender, direction, conversation fields).
- **Keep `destination_caller_id` optional** per imsg payload contract.
- **Fail-closed** on incomplete/conflicting projections; **drop recovered `is_from_me: true` rows**.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `577af515`

| Layer | Case | Result |
|-------|------|--------|
| L1 | issue synthetic repro: stale sender → authoritative remote sender | pass |
| L1 | history omits `destination_caller_id` | pass |
| L1 | history `is_from_me: true` with notification `false` | dropped |
| L1 | conflicting exact-GUID rows | dropped |
| L2 | repair → inbound decision → `buildIMessageInboundContext` | `To=imessage:+15550000002` |
| L3 | `monitorIMessageProvider` + issue payloads: remote reply routing | `ctx.To=imessage:+15550000002` |
| L3 | `monitorIMessageProvider` + issue payloads: from-me suppression | dispatch count 0, runtime drop log |

### L3 — monitor whole-path proof (issue #104136 synthetic payloads)

Capture:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts -t "#104136" --reporter=verbose
```

```
[L3 proof #104136] scenario: stale local sender repaired to remote peer
[L3 proof #104136] anchorless notification sender: +15550000001
[L3 proof #104136] authoritative history sender: +15550000002
[L3 proof #104136] monitor dispatch ctx.To: imessage:+15550000002

[L3 proof #104136] scenario: authoritative from-me row suppressed before dispatch
[L3 proof #104136] notification is_from_me: false
[L3 proof #104136] history is_from_me: true
[L3 proof #104136] monitor dispatch count: 0
[L3 proof #104136] runtime error: imessage: dropping anchorless message GUID=11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111; recovered authoritative row is from-me
```

**Tests**

```

→ 13 passed
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts
→ 33 passed
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor.last-route.test.ts -t "#104136"
→ 2 passed
```
